newsitem.title: UK: UK stock exchange reviews order-book feedback.
newsitem.headline: UK stock exchange reviews order-book feedback.

text.p: A committee at the London Stock Exchange is reviewing industry reaction to new rules for order-driven electronic trading, sources close to the exchange said on Monday.

Member firms and other parties had until January 10 to give their comments on the new system to the exchange. Several hundred surveys were returned as part of the exchange's fine-tuning process, the sources said.
The exchange would not comment on the findings.

Order driven dealing, set to be launched in the fourth quarter of 1997, will automatically match buyers and sellers in Britain's top 100 stocks, replacing the current system where market makers set prices.

One of the most contentious issues surrounding the order book is the exchange's rule on reporting large block trades. Under the amendments published by the exchange last month, market makers will be permitted to delay reporting large block deals, even though other investors are obliged to reveal their transactions immediately.
